name: PRPP to IMP
description: Encodes de novo assembly of IMP, the common purine branchpoint that supplies both adenylate and guanylate biosynthesis and supports nucleotide production without relying solely on purine salvage.
notes: Atomic GIFT corresponding to the biologically bounded PRPP-to-IMP capability derived from KEGG M00048.

name: IMP to AMP
description: Encodes the adenylate-specific branch from IMP through adenylosuccinate to AMP, supplying the precursor of adenine nucleotides used in nucleic acids, energy transfer, and many cofactors.
notes: Atomic branch derived from KEGG M00049; ends at AMP because shared nucleotide phosphorylation is intentionally excluded.

name: IMP to GMP
description: Encodes the guanylate-specific branch that oxidizes IMP to XMP and aminates XMP to GMP, supplying the precursor of guanine nucleotides used in nucleic acids and GTP-dependent cellular processes.
notes: Atomic branch derived from KEGG M00050; ends at GMP because shared nucleotide phosphorylation is intentionally excluded.

name: Glutamine and PRPP to UMP
description: Encodes de novo assembly of UMP, the common precursor of uridine and cytidine nucleotides needed for RNA production, DNA precursor synthesis, and activated-sugar metabolism.
notes: Atomic GIFT corresponding to KEGG M00051; alternative dihydroorotate oxidation chemistries are separate routes.

name: UTP to CTP
description: Encodes CTP synthase-mediated amination of UTP to CTP, establishing cytidine nucleotide production for RNA synthesis and formation of activated intermediates in phospholipid and glycan biosynthesis.
notes: Atomic cytidylate-forming capability derived from KEGG M00052; shared UMP/UDP phosphorylation and CTP/CDP interconversion are intentionally excluded.

name: 3-phosphoglycerate to serine
description: Encodes de novo synthesis of L-serine from the glycolytic intermediate 3-phosphoglycerate, supplying the amino acid that also feeds glycine and both cysteine biosynthesis capabilities.
notes: Boundaries of KEGG M00020 retained. The phosphoserine phosphatase step is kept required even though a fifth of serA/serC genomes carry no recognised phosphatase orthologue; the chemistry is required and the missing reaction is reported rather than silently scored away.

name: Serine to glycine
description: Encodes serine hydroxymethyltransferase-mediated formation of glycine from L-serine, the dominant route to glycine and the main one-carbon donor reaction of the cell.
notes: No KEGG module covers this capability. Threonine aldolase is deliberately excluded as a route because it would require L-threonine as an input anchor and adds only 133 KEGG genomes beyond those carrying glyA.

name: Aspartate to aspartate 4-semialdehyde
description: Encodes activation and reduction of L-aspartate to L-aspartate 4-semialdehyde, the branchpoint metabolite shared by the lysine, diaminopimelate, threonine and methionine branches of the aspartate family.
notes: Shared head of KEGG M00018 and M00017, cut out so that neither module duplicates it. Anchored at the semialdehyde so the lysine and diaminopimelate branch can attach without re-cutting this GIFT.

name: Aspartate 4-semialdehyde to homoserine
description: Encodes homoserine dehydrogenase-mediated reduction of L-aspartate 4-semialdehyde to L-homoserine, the step that commits aspartate carbon away from lysine and towards threonine and methionine.
notes: Single-reaction GIFT shared by KEGG M00018 and M00017. It is not merged into the upstream GIFT because homoserine dehydrogenase is precisely where the lysine branch is left behind.

name: Homoserine to threonine
description: Encodes phosphorylation of L-homoserine and its conversion to L-threonine, establishing threonine identity after the aspartate family branchpoint.
notes: Tail of KEGG M00018; the aspartate-to-homoserine head is curated separately and composed through the homoserine anchor.

name: Homoserine and cysteine to methionine
description: Encodes methionine synthesis in which the sulfur is donated by L-cysteine through a cystathionine intermediate, the route used by organisms that assimilate sulfur into cysteine first.
notes: Tail of KEGG M00017. Separated from the sulfhydrylation capability because the two consume different sulfur substrates, and anchors are declared per GIFT rather than per route. L-homocysteine is deliberately internal here; see database_changes.

name: Homoserine and sulfide to methionine
description: Encodes methionine synthesis in which acylated homoserine reacts directly with inorganic sulfide, bypassing cysteine and cystathionine entirely.
notes: Absent from KEGG M00017 although 3910 KEGG genomes complete methionine biosynthesis this way and no other. giftr curation, not a KEGG import.

name: Serine and sulfide to cysteine
description: Encodes cysteine synthesis by acetylation of L-serine followed by sulfide incorporation, the principal route of sulfur assimilation into amino acids.
notes: Boundaries of KEGG M00021 retained; the sulfide requirement is declared explicitly as an input anchor so the capability can compose with assimilatory sulfate reduction.

name: Serine and homocysteine to cysteine
description: Encodes reverse transsulfuration, in which sulfur held in L-homocysteine is transferred through cystathionine onto a serine backbone to give L-cysteine.
notes: KEGG M00338 and the cysteine-forming tail of M00609 merged into one capability with two routes; their enzyme sets share no KEGG genome, which makes them alternatives rather than separate traits. The four SAM-cycle steps of M00609 are excluded.

name: D-xylose to D-xylulose 5-phosphate
description: Encodes isomerase-dependent catabolism of D-xylose to the pentose phosphate pathway, the route by which most gut and soil bacteria obtain carbon from hemicellulosic xylose.
notes: No KEGG module covers this capability. The oxidative Weimberg and Dahms routes end at different central metabolites and are therefore different capabilities, not alternative routes of this one.

name: L-arabinose to D-xylulose 5-phosphate
description: Encodes catabolism of L-arabinose released from arabinan and arabinoxylan side chains, converging on the same pentose phosphate entry point as xylose.
notes: Convergence on D-xylulose 5-phosphate is why arabinofuranosidase side-chain release composes with this GIFT rather than needing its own downstream chemistry.

name: L-fucose to dihydroxyacetone phosphate and (S)-lactaldehyde
description: Encodes isomerase-dependent catabolism of L-fucose, a deoxyhexose abundant in host mucin O-glycans, making it a marker of mucin foraging and cross-feeding in the gut.
notes: The oxidative dehydrogenase route yields different products and is a separate capability. Anchors are declared per GIFT, so the two cannot be routes of one trait.

name: L-rhamnose to dihydroxyacetone phosphate and (S)-lactaldehyde
description: Encodes catabolism of L-rhamnose, the deoxyhexose of pectic rhamnogalacturonan, through the same aldol cleavage chemistry as fucose but with distinct enzymes.
notes: Shares product anchors with fucose degradation but no reactions; the two isomerase, kinase and aldolase families are non-homologous.

name: beta-D-galactose to alpha-D-glucose 1-phosphate
description: Encodes the Leloir pathway, the dominant route for galactose released from lactose, plant galactans and host glycans.
notes: Boundaries of KEGG M00632 retained. Aldose 1-epimerase is optional because mutarotation also proceeds spontaneously; UDP-glucose 4-epimerase is required because without it the pathway cannot turn over catalytically.

name: N-acetyl-D-glucosamine to beta-D-fructose 6-phosphate
description: Encodes catabolism of N-acetyl-D-glucosamine released from chitin, peptidoglycan and host glycans into glycolysis.
notes: Ends at fructose 6-phosphate, the point at which amino sugar carbon becomes indistinguishable from glycolytic carbon.

name: N-acetylneuraminate to beta-D-fructose 6-phosphate
description: Encodes catabolism of sialic acid released from host mucin O-glycans, a capability tightly associated with gut colonisation and with cross-feeding on sialidase-producing neighbours.
notes: Shares the deacetylase and deaminase reactions with GlcNAc degradation but is not a composite of it: the shared intermediate is N-acetyl-D-glucosamine 6-phosphate, which is internal to both and is deliberately not an anchor.

name: D-galacturonate to pyruvate and D-glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate
description: Encodes catabolism of the pectin backbone residue D-galacturonate through the isomerase route into central carbon metabolism.
notes: Shares its final two reactions with glucuronate degradation; the uronate-specific head reactions differ and are what the two capabilities are about.

name: D-glucuronate to pyruvate and D-glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate
description: Encodes catabolism of D-glucuronate, released from glucuronoxylan and host glycosaminoglycans, into central carbon metabolism.
notes: Boundaries of KEGG M00061 retained.

name: D-xylose uptake
description: Encodes ATP-dependent import of D-xylose, the step that separates a genome able to consume xylose released by others from one that merely encodes the catabolic enzymes.
notes: Curated because D-xylose has both substrate-specific transporter markers and a Rhea master for the translocation. Sugars moved mainly by promiscuous carriers are deliberately left without an uptake GIFT.

name: L-arabinose uptake
description: Encodes ATP-dependent import of L-arabinose, distinguishing an arabinose cross-feeder from a genome carrying only the catabolic enzymes.
notes: As for xylose. The dual-specificity XacGHI system is accepted for both pentoses because it is characterised on both.

name: Xylan to D-xylose
description: Encodes saccharification of xylan to free D-xylose: endo-acting cleavage of the beta-1,4-xylose backbone followed by exo-acting release of the monosaccharide. A positive call means the genome can liberate usable xylose from the dominant hemicellulose of a plant-based diet.
notes: Endo- and exo-acting chemistry are both required for this curated saccharification capability. Endo-1,4-beta-xylanase depolymerises the xylan backbone and generates additional chain ends and xylo-oligosaccharides, while beta-xylosidase releases D-xylose successively from non-reducing termini. Although beta-xylosidase can in principle release xylose directly from xylan termini, exo activity alone is not treated here as sufficient evidence for complete polymer saccharification. Xylo-oligosaccharide is an internal intermediate, not an anchor: it would become one only if an oligosaccharide importer could be evidenced, which would make the selfish-foraging route independently meaningful.

name: Arabinoxylan to xylan and L-arabinose
description: Encodes removal of alpha-L-arabinofuranosyl decorations from arabinoxylan, releasing free L-arabinose and exposing the xylan backbone to the enzymes of xylan degradation.
notes: Kept separate from xylan degradation because L-arabinose is itself an anchored fermentable sugar, so the same arabinose GIFTs serve arabinoxylan, arabinan and arabinogalactan without triplicate curation. One reaction, but a complete capability with its own product.

name: Starch to D-glucose
description: Encodes saccharification of starch to free D-glucose: endo-acting cleavage of the alpha-1,4-glucan backbone followed by exo-acting release of the monosaccharide.
notes: Endo- and exo-acting chemistry are both required for this curated saccharification capability. Alpha-amylase depolymerises the alpha-1,4-glucan backbone and generates additional chain ends and malto-oligosaccharides, while alpha-glucosidase releases D-glucose successively from non-reducing termini. As for xylan, the exo-acting enzyme can in principle act on polymer termini directly, but exo activity alone is not treated here as sufficient evidence for complete polymer saccharification. Debranching is accessory rather than required: amylose carries no alpha-1,6 branch points, so a genome without pullulanase still degrades starch, less completely. Malto-oligosaccharide is an internal intermediate for the same reason as xylo-oligosaccharide.

name: Collagen to collagen peptides
description: Encodes cleavage of native triple-helical collagen, releasing collagen-derived peptides outside the cell. A positive call means the genome encodes a microbial collagenase of MEROPS family M9, the activity that degrades the intact helix; it does not mean the organism assimilates the peptides.
notes: One required reaction, but a complete capability with its own product, as for arabinoxylan debranching. Substrate specificity rests on mechanism rather than on a family name: EC 3.4.24.3 is defined by digestion of native collagen in the triple-helical region, which generic endopeptidases cannot perform because the intact helix resists them. Broadly proteolytic enzymes such as pseudolysin are deliberately excluded even though they hydrolyse collagen among other host proteins, because accepting them would equate this trait with generic proteolysis. The product anchor is substrate-specific rather than a shared peptide pool; a shared oligopeptide tier and peptide uptake are deferred behind transporter evidence.

name: Flagellar apparatus
description: Encodes the structural and assembly machinery of a bacterial flagellum: the type III export apparatus, basal body, C ring, hook, filament and stator of at least one curated flagellar architecture. A positive call means the genome encodes that machinery. It does not mean the organism is motile, that the flagellum is expressed, or that it rotates under any particular condition.
notes: Ion coupling is deliberately not claimed. KEGG assigns the sodium-driven PomA/PomB stator of Vibrio cholerae to K02556/K02557, the same orthologues as the proton-driven MotA/MotB stator of Escherichia coli, so KO evidence cannot separate proton- from sodium-driven motors. Separate proton_driven_flagellar_apparatus and sodium_driven_flagellar_apparatus GIFTs are therefore refused at this evidence level; see inst/doc/proposal-structural-gifts.md. Transcriptional regulators (FlhDC, FliA, FlgM) are excluded because they are regulatory, not structural.

name: Type IVa pilus machinery
description: Encodes the machinery required to assemble a type IVa pilus: prepilin processing, a major pilin, an extension ATPase, the inner membrane platform, the PilMNOP alignment subcomplex and the PilQ secretin. A positive call means the genome encodes that machinery; it does not establish twitching motility, natural competence, or adhesion to any particular surface, none of which follow from the assembly machinery alone.
notes: Scoped to the type IVa system because the alignment subcomplex markers (PilM/N/O/P) are specific to it; type IVb and Tad pili are different architectures and are not covered. Retraction is curated as an accessory function: a pilus can be assembled without PilT.

name: Chemotaxis signal transduction
description: Encodes the core chemotaxis signal-transduction machinery: a chemoreceptor, the CheA histidine kinase with its CheW coupling protein, the CheY response regulator, and the CheR/CheB adaptation cycle. A positive call means the genome encodes that pathway. It does not mean the cell is chemotactic, that the pathway is expressed, or that the organism responds to any particular compound: which chemoeffectors are detected depends on receptor sensing domains this claim says nothing about.
notes: The reception function accepts either a generic methyl-accepting chemotaxis protein (K03406) or any characterised chemoreceptor. Both are needed: Escherichia coli K-12 carries no K03406 orthologue at all, its four receptors being assigned to the characterised groups, while Pseudomonas aeruginosa carries 21 K03406 genes and Vibrio cholerae 34. Signal termination is accessory and has three non-homologous implementations (CheZ, CheC, CheX). CheV is not accepted as a CheW substitute. See inst/doc/proposal-regulatory-gifts.md.

name: Aspartate chemoreception
description: Encodes the machinery to detect L-aspartate and transduce it into the chemotaxis pathway: the Tar aspartate chemoreceptor together with the shared chemotaxis kinase, response-regulator and adaptation functions. A positive call means the genome encodes an aspartate-responsive chemosensory input. It does not mean the cell swims toward aspartate, which additionally requires expression, a working flagellar motor, and a gradient.
notes: This GIFT exists to keep the core pathway honest. Its reception function accepts K05875 (Tar) only. The generic chemoreceptor accession K03406 is deliberately refused here: it identifies the conserved cytoplasmic signalling domain shared by every chemoreceptor and cannot single out an aspartate sensor, so accepting it would let any chemotactic genome claim aspartate sensing. The three downstream functions are the same curated rows the core circuit uses.

name: Phosphate starvation response
description: Encodes a phosphate-starvation two-component regulatory system: the PhoR sensor histidine kinase paired with a cognate phosphate-regulon response regulator. A positive call means the genome encodes the signalling machinery. It does not mean the regulon is induced, that the cell is phosphate-limited, or that any particular gene is regulated.
notes: Two curated circuits share the PhoR sensor and differ in the response regulator: PhoB (K07657) in enterobacteria, pseudomonads and vibrios, PhoP (K07658) in Bacillus and relatives. Across the reference genomes checked on 2026-08-18 the sensor is single-copy where present and the two regulator groups are mutually exclusive, which is what licenses orthology as evidence of a cognate pair here. K07660, the response regulator of the magnesium-sensing PhoP/PhoQ system, shares the gene name and is a different protein; it is not accepted. The PstSCAB-PhoU complex is accessory because it is independently a transport capability.

name: Type I restriction-modification
description: Encodes a complete type I restriction-modification system: the HsdS specificity subunit, the HsdM methyltransferase that protects the host's own target sites, and the HsdR subunit that translocates and cleaves unmethylated DNA. A positive call means the genome encodes that mechanism. It does not mean the organism resists any particular phage, which depends on the invader's anti-restriction counter-measures and on defences this GIFT does not describe.
notes: All three subunits are required. A genome carrying only HsdM and HsdS has a methylation capability, which is real biology and common as an orphan methyltransferase, but it defends against nothing and is correctly called incomplete here. The target sequence the system recognises is deliberately not claimed: HsdS specificity comes from variable target recognition domains that the orthology group does not resolve.

name: Type I-E CRISPR-Cas machinery
description: Encodes the protein machinery of a type I-E CRISPR-Cas system: the five-subunit Cascade surveillance complex and the Cas3 nuclease-helicase, with Cas1-Cas2 spacer acquisition accessory. A positive call means the genome encodes those proteins. It does not mean the system can interfere with anything, because interference additionally requires a CRISPR array to supply guide RNAs, and an array is a repeat-spacer locus detected by structure rather than a protein annotation.
notes: The claim is deliberately narrowed to the encoded machinery. giftr's evidence layer is an annotation accession, which cannot express 'a CRISPR array was detected in this genome', and no Cas protein accession is evidence that an array is present. Broadening the evidence model to genomic features was considered and deferred to a second demonstrated need; see inst/doc/proposal-defense-gifts.md.

name: Pyruvate to acetyl-CoA
description: Encodes decarboxylation of pyruvate to acetyl-CoA, the step that connects every sugar and amino acid catabolism GIFT ending at pyruvate to acyl-CoA chemistry and to short-chain fatty acid formation.
notes: No KEGG module covers this capability as a unit. Three non-homologous routes are curated because they are not interchangeable: the dehydrogenase complex is the aerobic route, the ferredoxin oxidoreductase and formate-lyase routes are oxygen-sensitive, and 10961 of 11856 KEGG organisms complete at least one. The dehydrogenase reaction carries two alternative systems because the fused E1 of Escherichia coli (K00163) and the alpha/beta E1 of Bacillus (K00161 with K00162) are different architectures; requiring either alone would call roughly 4800 genomes negative for chemistry they have.

name: Acetyl-CoA and acetate interconversion
description: Encodes the two-step interconversion of acetyl-CoA and acetate through acetyl phosphate, the substrate-level phosphorylation that yields ATP when it runs towards acetate. A positive call means the genome encodes that chemistry. It does not mean the cell excretes acetate, and it cannot mean that: the same two enzymes run the reaction towards acetyl-CoA in genomes assimilating acetate, and no marker distinguishes the directions.
notes: Declared interconversion rather than catabolic because the node is near-equilibrium and physiologically bidirectional, and because a catabolic declaration would place any future acetate-activation GIFT in a within-mode cycle with this one. Boundaries of KEGG M00579 retained. 6582 of 11856 KEGG organisms complete it, so a positive call carries little discriminating power on its own; it is curated because it is the boundary the butyrate transferase route consumes.

name: Acetyl-CoA and acetate to butanoate
description: Encodes condensation and reduction of acetyl-CoA to butanoyl-CoA followed by CoA transfer onto acetate, releasing butanoate. A positive call means the genome encodes that route. It does not mean butyrate is produced, excreted, or ecologically consequential, and it says nothing about the amount.
notes: Absent from KEGG, and not curatable from KEGG orthology: the four core enzymes are chain-length-generic and the transferase shares K01034 and K01035 with the acetoacetate degradation transferase of Escherichia coli, so a KO-evidenced route calls Faecalibacterium prausnitzii, Roseburia intestinalis and Agathobacter rectalis negative and Bacillus subtilis positive. The terminal step is therefore evidenced by NCBIfam TIGR03948, corroborated by InterPro IPR023990 and HAMAP MF_03227. The butyrate kinase route is deliberately refused because Ptb and Buk are shared with Bacillus branched-chain acyl-CoA metabolism at KO and at TIGRFAM level alike. See inst/doc/proposal-scfa-biosynthesis.md.

name: (S)-lactaldehyde to (S)-propane-1,2-diol
description: Encodes reduction of the (S)-lactaldehyde released by deoxyhexose aldol cleavage to (S)-propane-1,2-diol, the step that converts fucose and rhamnose carbon into a diol that fermentation can carry to propionate.
notes: One reaction, but a complete capability with its own product, as for arabinoxylan debranching. Curated separately from the propionate route because propane-1,2-diol is itself a documented boundary metabolite: genomes carrying the propanediol utilisation operon frequently acquire the diol rather than making it, and 87 of the 232 such genomes carry no lactaldehyde reductase at all.

name: (S)-propane-1,2-diol to propanoate
description: Encodes dehydration of propane-1,2-diol to propanal, its oxidation to propanoyl-CoA, and substrate-level phosphorylation to propanoate. A positive call means the genome encodes that route, not that propionate is produced or released.
notes: No KEGG module covers this capability. 168 of 11856 KEGG organisms complete it and they are the propanediol utilisation operon of the Enterobacteriaceae: Salmonella (51), Klebsiella (46), Citrobacter (24), Yersinia (18) and Escherichia (9). The dehydratase is adenosylcobalamin-dependent; giftr models no cofactor availability, so the call does not assert that B12 is present.

name: (R)-lactate to propanoate
description: Encodes the acrylate pathway: CoA transfer onto lactate, dehydration to acryloyl-CoA, and reduction to propanoyl-CoA, with propanoyl-CoA regenerated as the CoA donor so that lactate is the net substrate and propanoate the net product.
notes: The most substrate-specific and least prevalent capability in this layer. All 13 KEGG organisms carrying propionate CoA-transferase with both lactoyl-CoA dehydratase subunits are characterised acrylate-pathway producers, among them Anaerotignum propionicum, Megasphaera elsdenii and Pseudocoprococcus catus, and no genome outside that group carries the set. The acryloyl-CoA reductase K20143 is assigned in only 4 of those 13, so most are reported incomplete with the reductase named as the missing reaction rather than having the step scored away; this follows the serine phosphatase precedent. The lcdC activator subunit has no orthology group and is not required.

name: Pyruvate to (S)-lactate
description: Encodes NAD-dependent reduction of pyruvate to (S)-lactate, the terminal disposal of reducing equivalents in homofermentative and mixed-acid fermentation. Unlike every other fermentation end product curated so far, the direction of this claim is evidenced rather than asserted: forming lactate is a cytoplasmic NADH-consuming reduction and consuming it feeds electrons to a quinone or a cytochrome, and KEGG assigns those to different orthology groups.
notes: K00016 is present in 4143 of the 11855 KEGG organisms examined and the quinone-dependent lldD group K29125 in 3388, but only 573 carry both. Every lactic acid bacterium checked carries the forming group and not the consuming one, and Escherichia coli, Salmonella Typhimurium and Pseudomonas aeruginosa are the reverse. The quinone- and cytochrome-dependent groups K29125, K00101, K03777 and K00102 are deliberately not accepted as markers, because they evidence the opposite direction. D-lactate formation is not curated: K03778 is specific to the right chemistry but its leading genera are Pseudomonas, Streptomyces and Burkholderia, which run the reaction oxidatively, and the (R) anchor is reached through lactate_racemisation instead.

name: (S)-lactate and (R)-lactate interconversion
description: Encodes lactate racemase, which interconverts the two lactate enantiomers. A positive call means the genome can supply either enantiomer from the other. It does not mean the cell prefers a direction, and it cannot mean that: a racemase has no direction to prefer.
notes: Declared interconversion rather than catabolic because a racemase is the purest instance of that mode: acetate_interconversion is reversible as a matter of physiology, LarA as a matter of definition. It resolves a defect the SCFA layer left behind. propionate_formation_acrylate consumes (R)-lactate and nothing produced it, and of the ten KEGG genomes behind that route eight carry K22373 while only two carry a D-lactate dehydrogenase, so the racemase is how those organisms actually reach the anchor.

name: (S)-malate to (S)-lactate
description: Encodes malolactic enzyme, the direct decarboxylation of (S)-malate to (S)-lactate without a free pyruvate intermediate. This is the only capability in the database that takes a citric acid cycle metabolite as a boundary, and it takes it as an input.
notes: K22212 is present in 337 organisms and the set is Streptococcus, Lacticaseibacillus, Enterococcus, Lactococcus, Limosilactobacillus, Lactiplantibacillus, Lactobacillus and Leuconostoc almost without exception. The step releases CO2 and is therefore irreversible, which is why malate may be a boundary here while fumarase and malate dehydrogenase license no malate-forming trait.

name: Citrate to pyruvate and acetate
description: Encodes fermentative cleavage of citrate: the holo-citrate lyase complex splits citrate to oxaloacetate and acetate, and oxaloacetate is decarboxylated to pyruvate. A positive call means the genome encodes the chemistry, not that it expresses it; the classic aerobic citrate-utilisation phenotype is a transport and regulation phenotype that giftr does not model.
notes: The lyase with its activating ligase is complete in 912 of 11855 organisms and adding an oxaloacetate decarboxylase gives 369, led by Salmonella, Streptococcus, Klebsiella, Lacticaseibacillus and Enterococcus. Bacillus subtilis, Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron and Pseudomonas aeruginosa are negative. Oxaloacetate is an internal intermediate and is deliberately not an anchor. The citrate transporter is not required evidence: Escherichia coli K-12 carries CitT and is aerobically Cit-negative because the gene is not expressed under oxygen, so requiring it would look like a phenotype claim without being one.

name: Acetyl-CoA to ethanol
description: Encodes the bifunctional acetaldehyde/alcohol dehydrogenase route from acetyl-CoA to ethanol, in which one protein carries both reductions. A positive call means the genome encodes that chemistry; AdhE is reversible and is used in the ethanol-oxidising direction by some genomes, and no marker distinguishes the two.
notes: K04072 is present in 2519 organisms, led by Streptococcus, Vibrio, Bacillus, Escherichia, Clostridium and Bifidobacterium. The route deliberately does not cover Zymomonas mobilis or Saccharomyces cerevisiae, which decarboxylate pyruvate through K01568 with a separate alcohol dehydrogenase; that route is complete in 258 organisms, is fungus-dominated, and its bacterial tail is Acetobacter and Gluconobacter, which oxidise ethanol rather than form it. It is left for a later pass rather than curated as an equal alternative.

name: Pyruvate to (R)-acetoin
description: Encodes condensation of two pyruvate to (2S)-2-acetolactate and its decarboxylation to (R)-acetoin, the neutral fermentation route that the Voges-Proskauer test detects. The trait rests on the decarboxylase, which has no other role.
notes: K01575 is present in 1649 organisms, led by Streptococcus, Bacillus, Corynebacterium, Staphylococcus, Klebsiella, Enterobacter, Listeria, Enterococcus and Lactococcus. The synthase step is curated but not required, because its orthology group K01652 is the anabolic branched-chain amino acid synthase ilvB/ilvG/ilvI and carries no acetoin-specific information; requiring it changes the call in 50 of 1649 genomes and imports a marker that means something else. Butane-2,3-diol is one step further and is not curated.

name: GTP and D-ribulose 5-phosphate to riboflavin
description: Encodes de novo synthesis of riboflavin (vitamin B2) from GTP and D-ribulose 5-phosphate: ring opening and reduction of the GTP-derived pyrimidinedione, condensation with the four-carbon unit to give dimethylribityllumazine, and dismutation to riboflavin. A positive call means the genome encodes that route. It does not mean riboflavin is exported or available to anything else.
notes: Boundary ends at riboflavin. The flavin kinase and FMN adenylyltransferase that make FMN and FAD are shared housekeeping, complete in every reference genome including those that cannot make riboflavin, and are deliberately not curated.

name: Chorismate to 4-aminobenzoate
description: Encodes synthesis of 4-aminobenzoate from chorismate through 4-amino-4-deoxychorismate. A positive call means the genome can make the aromatic half of folate for itself; a negative one identifies a genome that must acquire 4-aminobenzoate, which is a documented dependency of several gut lineages.
notes: Cut from folate biosynthesis because the two halves are separately lost: 4099 KEGG bacteria complete both branches, 1799 only the pterin branch and 989 only this one.

name: GTP and 4-aminobenzoate to tetrahydrofolate
description: Encodes de novo synthesis of tetrahydrofolate (vitamin B9) from GTP and 4-aminobenzoate: pterin ring formation, coupling to 4-aminobenzoate, glutamylation and reduction. A positive call means the genome encodes that route; it says nothing about how much folate is made or whether any leaves the cell.
notes: Two dephosphorylation steps between the pterin triphosphate and dihydroneopterin are not gating. The pyrophosphatase is curated as not required because its orthology is Proteobacteria-biased; the residual monophosphatase step is not curated at all, because the only marker offered for it is a generic alkaline phosphatase that would fire in every genome.

name: AIR to the thiamine pyrimidine
description: Encodes de novo synthesis of the thiamine pyrimidine moiety: radical SAM rearrangement of the purine intermediate AIR into hydroxymethylpyrimidine phosphate, and its phosphorylation to the diphosphate that thiamine phosphate synthase requires.
notes: AIR is declared as an input anchor only. Purine core biosynthesis does not declare it as an output, so no composition edge is created from an internal purine intermediate.

name: DXP to the thiamine thiazole
description: Encodes de novo synthesis of the thiamine thiazole moiety from 1-deoxy-D-xylulose 5-phosphate and an imine donor. A positive call means the genome encodes thiazole synthase together with an enzyme that supplies 2-iminoacetate.
notes: ThiS and ThiF are not required components. ThiF is homologous to MoeB and ThiI also serves tRNA thiolation, so neither marker adds thiamine specificity, while requiring them would reduce the trait from 5396 to 1554 bacterial genomes.

name: Thiamine pyrimidine and thiazole to thiamine phosphate
description: Encodes condensation of the two thiamine moieties into thiamine phosphate (vitamin B1). A positive call means the genome encodes thiamine phosphate synthase; combined with the two branch GIFTs it means de novo thiamine synthesis, and combined with the salvage GIFT it means the genome can build thiamine from acquired precursors.
notes: The boundary stops at thiamine phosphate rather than the diphosphate. ThiL is absent from the KEGG annotation of ten of eighteen reference genomes that certainly make TPP, so requiring it would turn an annotation gap into an auxotrophy call.

name: Thiamine precursor salvage to the activated moieties
description: Encodes phosphorylation of the free thiamine pyrimidine and thiazole acquired from the environment, giving the same two activated moieties that de novo synthesis produces. A positive call identifies a genome that can build thiamine from precursors made by something else.
notes: Curated as a separate capability that composes with thiamine phosphate biosynthesis through the HMP_PP and THZ_P anchors, so that ThiE is curated once rather than duplicated into a salvage route.

name: 2-oxoisovalerate and L-aspartate to pantothenate
description: Encodes de novo synthesis of pantothenate (vitamin B5): hydroxymethylation and reduction of the branched-chain 2-oxo acid to pantoate, decarboxylation of L-aspartate to beta-alanine, and their ligation. A positive call means the genome encodes that route.
notes: The boundary stops at pantothenate. The five steps that convert it to coenzyme A are shared housekeeping and are not curated. KEGG M00119 defines completeness without PanC or PanD and therefore never reaches pantothenate.

name: Ribose 5-phosphate and glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate to pyridoxal 5-phosphate
description: Encodes the DXP-independent route to pyridoxal 5-phosphate (vitamin B6): a single PdxS/PdxT synthase complex builds the pyridine ring from a pentose phosphate, a triose phosphate and the amide nitrogen of glutamine. A positive call means the genome encodes that complex.
notes: Separate from the DXP-dependent capability because the input boundaries differ, following the precedent of the two methionine biosynthesis GIFTs. The two routes are near-disjoint across bacteria and together cover 4199 genomes.

name: Erythrose 4-phosphate and DXP to pyridoxal 5-phosphate
description: Encodes the DXP-dependent route to pyridoxal 5-phosphate (vitamin B6), in which erythrose 4-phosphate is oxidised and transaminated to 4-phosphohydroxy-L-threonine, decarboxylated, condensed with 1-deoxy-D-xylulose 5-phosphate to pyridoxine 5-phosphate, and oxidised to the aldehyde.
notes: Shares phosphoserine aminotransferase with serine biosynthesis. The marker is accepted for this reaction, not as evidence of vitamin B6 synthesis on its own; the other five reactions carry the claim.

name: Pimeloyl-CoA to biotin
description: Encodes assembly of the biotin bicyclic ring from a pimelate thioester: condensation with L-alanine, transamination, ring closure to dethiobiotin, and sulfur insertion by biotin synthase. A positive call means the genome encodes that route.
notes: The precursor supply that makes the pimelate thioester is deliberately not curated: BioC/BioH, BioI, BioW and BioU are non-homologous solutions and no marker set spans them. The thioester carrier is not distinguished by the BioF marker, so the claim covers both the CoA and the acyl-carrier-protein forms.

name: L-aspartate to quinolinate
description: Encodes de novo formation of the pyridine ring of NAD from L-aspartate and dihydroxyacetone phosphate. A positive call means the genome can build the ring rather than depending on an exogenous pyridine.
notes: Cut at quinolinate so that de novo ring formation and pyridine salvage are separate claims that share no reactions.

name: Quinolinate to nicotinate D-ribonucleotide
description: Encodes phosphoribosyl transfer onto quinolinate with decarboxylation, giving nicotinate D-ribonucleotide. This is the step at which de novo pyridine synthesis joins the shared nucleotide chemistry that both salvage and cobamide lower-ligand attachment also use.
notes: Curated as its own GIFT so that the de novo and salvage capabilities can share the downstream adenylylation and amidation without duplicating them.

name: Nicotinate D-ribonucleotide to NAD
description: Encodes adenylylation of nicotinate D-ribonucleotide and amidation of the resulting deamido-NAD to NAD. A positive call means the genome completes the shared trunk that both de novo synthesis and pyridine salvage feed.
notes: Shared by the de novo and salvage capabilities, which is why it is curated once rather than repeated in both.

name: Nicotinate to nicotinate D-ribonucleotide
description: Encodes recovery of an exogenous pyridine ring: nicotinate phosphoribosyltransferase converts acquired nicotinate into nicotinate D-ribonucleotide, which the shared trunk carries to NAD. A positive call means the genome can live on niacin; it does not mean the genome can make the ring.
notes: The layer separates being able to use vitamin B3 from being able to make it. 6921 KEGG bacteria carry this salvage together with the trunk, against 6398 that can form quinolinate from aspartate.

name: Uroporphyrinogen III to cobyrinate a,c-diamide
description: Encodes construction of the cobalt-loaded corrin ring from the tetrapyrrole branchpoint, by either the aerobic or the anaerobic route. A positive call means the genome encodes de novo corrin synthesis, which is the step that separates a corrinoid producer from a corrinoid salvager.
notes: Recall is limited by gene fusion: Propionibacterium freudenreichii carries cysG_cbiX and a cobJ_cbiE_cbiG_cbiH fusion that KEGG assigns to none of the component orthology groups, so the industrial B12 producer is called incomplete with three named missing reactions. Pfam PF00590 covers every cobalt-precorrin methyltransferase and cannot resolve the individual steps, so no domain marker rescues it.

name: Cobyrinate a,c-diamide to adenosylcobinamide phosphate
description: Encodes adenosylation of the corrin ring, amidation of its remaining carboxylates, and attachment of the aminopropanol arm, giving the adenosylcobinamide phosphate that lower-ligand assembly requires.
notes: Curated separately from the ring because the two are separately present: 4428 KEGG bacteria carry this chemistry against 1081 that also complete a corrin ring.

name: Adenosylcobinamide phosphate and dimethylbenzimidazole to cobalamin
description: Encodes assembly of the cobamide nucleotide loop: guanylylation of adenosylcobinamide phosphate, transfer of the lower ligand onto nicotinate D-ribonucleotide, dephosphorylation, and joining of the two halves to give adenosylcobalamin. A positive call means the genome can attach a lower ligand; with 5,6-dimethylbenzimidazole as the ligand the product is vitamin B12, and 3044 bacteria carrying this capability encode no corrin ring at all, so a positive call is not evidence of production.
notes: Declares nicotinate D-ribonucleotide as an input anchor because CobT consumes it, which is what connects the cobamide layer to NAD metabolism. The CobU kinase half of the bifunctional marker is what lets a salvager enter this capability from imported cobinamide.

name: FMNH2 to 5,6-dimethylbenzimidazole
description: Encodes the oxygen-dependent BluB route to 5,6-dimethylbenzimidazole, the lower ligand that makes a cobamide into vitamin B12. A negative call does not establish that the genome cannot make the ligand: the anaerobic bza route has no orthology group and is not curated.
notes: FMNH2 is declared as an input-only anchor. BluB destroys the flavin to build the benzimidazole ring, which is the one case in this layer where a cofactor is a substrate rather than a recycled participant.

name: Chorismate to menaquinone
description: Encodes synthesis of menaquinone (vitamin K2) from chorismate, by either the classical men route or the futalosine route. A positive call means the genome encodes one complete route to the prenylated, methylated naphthoquinone.
notes: Two orphan steps are curated as not required: MenH, whose elimination also proceeds without a dedicated enzyme, and the DHNA-CoA thioesterase, which has several non-homologous replacements and no orthology group covering them. Requiring both would reduce the classical route from 3109 to 1355 bacterial genomes.

name: Acetyl-CoA and oxaloacetate to isocitrate
description: Encodes condensation of acetyl-CoA with oxaloacetate to citrate and isomerisation to isocitrate by citrate synthase and aconitase. Isocitrate is exposed as the branchpoint between oxidative decarboxylation and the glyoxylate bypass. A positive call means this upper central-carbon segment is encoded; it does not mean either downstream fate or either derived cycle is complete.
notes: Re-cut from acetyl_coa_to_oxoglutarate so that the oxidative and glyoxylate branches do not duplicate citrate synthase and aconitase. K01659 remains accepted at ambiguous confidence because it contains genuine citrate synthases as well as 2-methylcitrate synthases. K01681, K01682 and K27802 remain alternative aconitase markers. Full assessment in inst/doc/proposal-central-metabolic-cycles.md.

name: 2-oxoglutarate to succinate
description: Encodes the oxidative conversion of 2-oxoglutarate to succinate by any of three alternative implementations: the 2-oxoglutarate dehydrogenase complex, the ferredoxin-dependent 2-oxoglutarate oxidoreductase, or the 2-oxoglutarate decarboxylase bypass through succinate semialdehyde. Succinyl-CoA and succinate semialdehyde are internal intermediates.
notes: The dehydrogenase complex is complete in 6902 organisms, the ferredoxin oxidoreductase in 3288 and the decarboxylase bypass in 1420; 8932 complete at least one. The bypass is the actinobacterial substitution that makes Mycobacterium tuberculosis and Corynebacterium glutamicum positive although both lack the E1o component. Direction is claimed for the GIFT as a whole and is honest for the dehydrogenase and decarboxylase routes, both of which release CO2 irreversibly; the ferredoxin route is the reductive citric acid cycle enzyme and is genuinely reversible, so its direction is a route-level claim the markers do not independently support. Making mode route-scoped is recorded as open question Q2 of inst/doc/proposal-central-metabolic-cycles.md. Succinyl-CoA synthetase is curated as one reaction with two enzyme systems rather than as separate ADP- and GDP-forming reactions, because K01899 and K01900 carry both EC numbers and no marker separates them.

name: Succinate and fumarate interconversion
description: Encodes the quinone-dependent interconversion of succinate and fumarate. The mode is interconversion and not a direction, because succinate dehydrogenase and fumarate reductase are the same orthology group in most bacteria. A positive call states that the genome encodes the couple, not which way it runs, and it is not a claim about fumarate respiration.
notes: K00239 is named by KEGG sdhA, frdA and K00240 sdhB, frdB: one group for both enzymes, present in 8047 organisms. The dedicated frdAB group K00244/K00245 exists in 1059, almost all Enterobacteriaceae, and 943 of the 1041 genomes carrying frdABCD also carry sdhABCD, so the split is a paralogue duplication within one clade rather than a functional partition. Two opposed directional GIFTs would therefore be complete on identical markers in 8047 genomes. Only the catalytic flavoprotein and iron-sulfur subunits are required; requiring the cytochrome b anchor K00241 as well would call a further 402 genomes negative on a poorly conserved membrane subunit. The generic quinone reaction RHEA:40523 is curated rather than the ubiquinone, menaquinone or rhodoquinone forms, because no marker distinguishes them; resolving that is the trigger recorded for splitting this GIFT.

name: Fumarate and oxaloacetate interconversion
description: Encodes hydration of fumarate to (S)-malate and oxidation of (S)-malate to oxaloacetate, or the reverse. Malate is an internal intermediate of this GIFT and remains an input-only boundary elsewhere. The mode is interconversion because fumarase is a hydratase at equilibrium and NAD-dependent malate dehydrogenase runs towards malate in every genome using the reductive branch.
notes: Fumarase is present in 10618 organisms and malate dehydrogenase or malate:quinone oxidoreductase in 9752; 9533 carry both. Rhea writes RHEA:12460 as (S)-malate = fumarate + H2O, so the traversal curated here records the hydratase step as reverse. Only malate:quinone oxidoreductase is effectively unidirectional towards oxaloacetate and it is one alternative system out of four, which is why the GIFT as a whole may not claim a direction. Splitting this GIFT at malate was assessed and deferred until a better-evidenced malate producer exists; see open question Q5 of inst/doc/proposal-central-metabolic-cycles.md.

name: Phosphoenolpyruvate and erythrose 4-phosphate to chorismate
description: Encodes the shikimate pathway, the seven-step condensation and reduction sequence that builds chorismate from two central carbon intermediates. Chorismate is the branchpoint at which aromatic metabolism leaves central metabolism: phenylalanine, tyrosine, tryptophan, 4-aminobenzoate, menaquinone, salicylate and the enterobactin aryl group all descend from it, which is why the capability ends there rather than at any one of them.
notes: Boundaries chosen independently of KEGG M00022, which shares them. The archaeal route to 3-dehydroquinate from 6-deoxy-5-ketofructose 1-phosphate and aspartate semialdehyde is deliberately outside this GIFT: it consumes different precursors, so it cannot be a route between these anchors.

name: Chorismate to salicylate
description: Encodes the isochorismate-dependent formation of salicylate from chorismate. In bacteria salicylate is a siderophore building block rather than an end product, and the capability stops at the free acid because the ligases that commit it to pyochelin, yersiniabactin or mycobactin are separate, siderophore-specific chemistry.
notes: One route of two reactions. PchA/PchB and the bifunctional salicylate synthases MbtI, Irp9 and YbtS run the same two transformations, so they are curated as alternative enzyme systems rather than as alternative routes.

name: L-tryptophan to indole-3-acetate
description: Encodes the indole-3-acetamide route from tryptophan to the auxin indole-3-acetate. Cut at tryptophan rather than at chorismate because tryptophan is a branchpoint and a building block in its own right, and bundling aromatic amino acid biosynthesis into an auxin trait would make two independently useful capabilities inseparable.
notes: Only the IAM route is curated. The indole-3-pyruvate, tryptamine, indole-3-acetonitrile and tryptophan side-chain oxidase routes are refused for want of markers that discriminate the activity; see inst/doc/proposal-shikimate-aromatics.md.

name: Urate to allantoin
description: Encodes oxidative opening of the purine ring of urate to allantoin: hydroxylation of urate to 5-hydroxyisourate and its hydrolysis and decarboxylation to (S)-allantoin. A positive call means the genome can begin mineralising host purine nitrogen. It does not mean the nitrogen is released as ammonium, which needs two further capabilities.

name: Allantoin to glyoxylate and urea
description: Encodes hydrolysis of allantoin to glyoxylate and urea, by either the allantoicase route or the allantoate deiminase route. A positive call means the genome can consume allantoin whether or not it can make it: 774 of the 893 bacteria completing this capability carry no uricase of any kind, so this is a consumer trait as often as a continuation of urate catabolism.
notes: Route-specific nitrogen fate: the deiminase route additionally releases two ammonium, the allantoicase route none. AMMONIUM is therefore not a declared output, because a GIFT anchor must hold for every route.

name: Urea to ammonium
description: Encodes urease-mediated hydrolysis of urea to ammonium and hydrogencarbonate. A positive call means the genome encodes the nickel-dependent urease catalytic core. It does not mean urea is available, nor that the ammonium is assimilated, nor that the pH rise urease causes is physiologically relevant.
notes: The UreD, UreE, UreF and UreG maturation proteins are deliberately not curated as components of the catalytic system. They perform nickel insertion rather than catalysis, and requiring all four drops the capability from 3725 to 2741 bacteria.

name: Nitrate to ammonium
description: Encodes assimilatory reduction of nitrate to ammonium: nitrate to nitrite by an assimilatory nitrate reductase, then nitrite to ammonium by a ferredoxin- or NAD(P)H-dependent nitrite reductase. A positive call means the genome can use nitrate as a nitrogen source. It is not a claim about nitrate respiration, denitrification or dissimilatory reduction, none of which giftr models, because giftr models no electron acceptors.
notes: Mode is anabolic on the SULFIDE precedent: assimilable inorganic nutrients enter giftr as inputs to anabolic capabilities. A fifth assimilatory mode was considered and deferred.

name: Glycine betaine to sarcosine
description: Encodes oxidative demethylation of glycine betaine to sarcosine through N,N-dimethylglycine. Every curated route is aerobic, because the first step is a Rieske monooxygenase that consumes molecular oxygen. A positive call means that chemistry is encoded; the anaerobic betaine reductase route to trimethylamine is a different capability and is not curated.

name: Sarcosine to glycine
description: Encodes demethylation of sarcosine to glycine, by the oxygen-dependent sarcosine oxidases or by the ferredoxin-dependent dehydrogenase. This is the shared tail of betaine and creatinine catabolism, curated once and reached from both by composition rather than duplicated in either.

name: Creatinine to sarcosine and urea
description: Encodes hydrolysis of creatinine to creatine and its cleavage to sarcosine and urea. A positive call requires both enzymes: 2431 bacteria carry the creatininase fold and only 194 also carry creatinase, so the first enzyme alone would over-call the capability more than tenfold.
notes: The creatinine deiminase route is refused: K01485 is a cytosine/creatinine deaminase, one accession for two activities, and the cytosine activity is the common one.

name: L-carnitine to trimethylamine
description: Encodes carnitine monooxygenase, the Rieske oxygenase that cleaves L-carnitine to trimethylamine and a four-carbon aldehyde. A positive call means the genome encodes that chemistry. It does not mean trimethylamine is produced or released, and it says nothing about host trimethylamine N-oxide, which requires a host flavin monooxygenase giftr does not model.

name: L-carnitine to glycine betaine
description: Encodes the dehydrogenase route from L-carnitine to glycine betaine: oxidation to 3-dehydrocarnitine, acetyl-CoA-dependent retro-Claisen cleavage to betainyl-CoA, and thioester hydrolysis. This route releases no trimethylamine, which is why it is a separate capability from carnitine monooxygenase rather than a second route of it.
notes: The betainyl-CoA thioesterase step is curated with required = 0. Its only marker, K27497, is a bifunctional protein that also carries the first step, and requiring it drops the capability from 944 to 256 bacteria.

name: Methylamine to ammonium
description: Encodes methylamine dehydrogenase, the tryptophan-tryptophylquinone enzyme that oxidises methylamine to formaldehyde and ammonium. Both subunits are jointly required. Formaldehyde is left as an internal product: it is a transient the cell detoxifies immediately and giftr has no consumer for it.
notes: The N-methylglutamate route is deferred: its four jointly required subunits complete in 46 bacteria, where single missing annotations would dominate the call.

name: Taurine to sulfite
description: Encodes taurine dioxygenase, the 2-oxoglutarate-dependent enzyme that releases the sulfonate sulfur of taurine as sulfite. A positive call means the genome can obtain sulfur from taurine. It leaves the nitrogen on aminoacetaldehyde and makes no nitrogen claim, and it is not a claim that hydrogen sulfide is formed.

name: Taurine to sulfite through sulfoacetaldehyde
description: Encodes removal of the taurine amino group by transamination or dehydrogenation and cleavage of the resulting sulfoacetaldehyde to acetyl phosphate and sulfite. A positive call means the genome encodes that chemistry. It is emphatically not a claim that hydrogen sulfide is produced: reducing sulfite to sulfide is dissimilatory sulfite reduction, which is respiration and out of scope.
notes: The nitrogen fate differs by route -- L-alanine from the transaminase, ammonium from the dehydrogenase -- so neither is a declared output and the GIFT makes no nitrogen claim. Acetyl phosphate is left internal rather than declared.

name: Taurine uptake
description: Encodes ATP-dependent import of taurine by the TauABC periplasmic-binding-protein-dependent transporter, the step that separates a genome able to consume taurine released by bile-salt hydrolysis from one that merely encodes the desulfonation enzymes.

name: Ammonium and 2-oxoglutarate to glutamate
description: Encodes assimilation of ammonium into glutamate, by the glutamine synthetase/glutamate synthase cycle or by glutamate dehydrogenase. A positive call is uninformative on its own, since 9482 of 10151 bacteria have it; the informative call is the negative one, which identifies genomes dependent on preformed amino acids. The capability exists in giftr so that ammonium is a boundary with a consumer rather than a terminal one.

name: Benzoate to catechol
description: Encodes ring dihydroxylation of benzoate and decarboxylating rearomatisation to catechol, the entry most aerobic peripheral aromatic routes use to reach the ring-cleavage node. A positive call means the genome encodes one complete curated route. It does not mean the compound is encountered, taken up, degraded in situ, or degraded at any rate. The benzoate 1,2-dioxygenase orthologues KEGG names benA and benB are benzoate/toluate enzymes: the call is honest for benzoate, which is within the enzyme's range, and for that reason no separate methylbenzoate or xylene-derived GIFT may be curated on the same markers, since the two traits would be indistinguishable.
notes: The markers are orthology groups for the substrate-determining subunits; the shared ferredoxin and ferredoxin reductase components of the same system are deliberately not required, because they are interchangeable between systems and are annotated two to three times less often than the subunits they serve, so requiring them would report an annotation gap as a missing capability.

name: Anthranilate to catechol
description: Encodes oxidative deamination and decarboxylation of anthranilate to catechol in one step, a second peripheral entry into the ring-cleavage node. Anthranilate is a kynurenine-pathway catabolite of tryptophan in host and microbe alike rather than an industrial compound. A positive call means the genome encodes one complete curated route. It does not mean the compound is encountered, taken up, degraded in situ, or degraded at any rate.
notes: The markers are orthology groups for the substrate-determining subunits; the shared ferredoxin and ferredoxin reductase components of the same system are deliberately not required, because they are interchangeable between systems and are annotated two to three times less often than the subunits they serve, so requiring them would report an annotation gap as a missing capability. Two alternative systems are curated, the antAB and andAcAd oxygenases, because they are non-homologous solutions annotated to different orthology groups.

name: Phenol to catechol
description: Encodes hydroxylation of phenol to catechol by the multicomponent phenol 2-monooxygenase. Phenol is a product of microbial tyrosine fermentation as well as an industrial compound. A positive call means the genome encodes one complete curated route. It does not mean the compound is encountered, taken up, degraded in situ, or degraded at any rate. KEGG module M00548 attaches the same marker set to benzene oxidation as well; that claim is not made here, because the enzyme is a phenol hydroxylase and giftr has no marker that evidences benzene as the substrate.
notes: All six subunits of the dmp/pox/tom system are jointly required. Unlike the Rieske systems in this layer, these components are the enzyme rather than interchangeable electron carriers.

name: Catechol to 3-oxoadipate by ortho cleavage
description: Encodes intradiol cleavage of catechol between the hydroxyls and conversion of the muconate through two lactones to 3-oxoadipate: the beta-ketoadipate pathway. A positive call means the genome encodes one complete curated route. It does not mean the compound is encountered, taken up, degraded in situ, or degraded at any rate. Ortho and meta cleavage are curated as separate GIFTs rather than alternative routes of one, because they produce different compounds and reach central metabolism at different points.
notes: The lactone hydrolysis step carries two alternative systems, the standalone pcaD hydrolase and the fused pcaL protein that also decarboxylates.

name: 3-Oxoadipate to 3-oxoadipyl-CoA
description: Encodes CoA transfer from succinyl-CoA onto 3-oxoadipate, the activation step that commits the ortho-cleavage product to thiolysis. A positive call means the genome encodes one complete curated route. It does not mean the compound is encountered, taken up, degraded in situ, or degraded at any rate.
notes: Curated as its own GIFT because 3-oxoadipyl-CoA is where the ortho-cleavage funnel and the aerobic phenylacetate route converge, and duplicating either segment inside the other would break composition through declared anchors.

name: 3-Oxoadipyl-CoA to succinyl-CoA and acetyl-CoA
description: Encodes thiolytic cleavage of 3-oxoadipyl-CoA, the single step that delivers aromatic carbon into central metabolism. A positive call means the genome encodes one complete curated route. It does not mean the compound is encountered, taken up, degraded in situ, or degraded at any rate.
notes: The thiolase orthologue is shared with the phenylacetate route, which is why it is curated once here rather than inside each upstream GIFT.

name: Catechol to 2-oxopent-4-enoate by meta cleavage
description: Encodes extradiol cleavage of catechol adjacent to the hydroxyls and conversion of the resulting semialdehyde to 2-oxopent-4-enoate, by either the hydrolytic or the 4-oxalocrotonate branch. A positive call means the genome encodes one complete curated route. It does not mean the compound is encountered, taken up, degraded in situ, or degraded at any rate.
notes: K07104 is deliberately refused as evidence of catechol 2,3-dioxygenase. It is assigned in 2081 KEGG genomes dominated by Bacillus, Streptococcus, Staphylococcus and Listeria, only 276 of which carry any lower meta pathway gene, and accepting it would put an over-broad marker in reach of every future GIFT that declares this activity. K00446 is used instead, corroborated by NCBIfam TIGR03211.

name: 2-Oxopent-4-enoate to pyruvate and acetyl-CoA
description: Encodes hydration, retro-aldol cleavage and acylating oxidation of 2-oxopent-4-enoate to pyruvate and acetyl-CoA. This is the common lower route of meta cleavage, shared by catechol, dihydroxyphenylpropanoate and, where their evidence permits, the biphenyl, cumate and xylene routes. A positive call means the genome encodes one complete curated route. It does not mean the compound is encountered, taken up, degraded in situ, or degraded at any rate.
notes: Curated once as an atomic GIFT rather than duplicated inside every upper route that ends here, which is what composition through declared anchors is for. Two alternative system sets are curated per step, the mhp and the bph/xyl/tes enzymes.

name: Phenylacetate to 3-oxoadipyl-CoA
description: Encodes the aerobic CoA-dependent route: activation of phenylacetate to its CoA thioester, epoxidation of the ring, isomerisation to the oxepin, hydrolytic ring opening, and beta-oxidation to 3-oxoadipyl-CoA. Phenylacetate is a phenylalanine fermentation product, which makes this the entry into the layer that host-associated genomes most often carry. A positive call means the genome encodes one complete curated route. It does not mean the compound is encountered, taken up, degraded in situ, or degraded at any rate.
notes: Ends at 3-oxoadipyl-CoA so that the terminal thiolysis is not duplicated: oxoadipyl_coa_thiolysis carries it once for this route and for the ortho-cleavage funnel alike. The route's last three steps use chain-generic beta-oxidation orthologues, one of which is already curated for butyrate formation; the specificity of the claim rests on paaK and the epoxidase, not on the tail.

name: 3-Phenylpropanoate to 3-(2,3-dihydroxyphenyl)propanoate
description: Encodes ring dihydroxylation of 3-phenylpropanoate and dehydrogenation of the diol to the catecholic phenylpropanoid. A positive call means the genome encodes one complete curated route. It does not mean the compound is encountered, taken up, degraded in situ, or degraded at any rate. trans-Cinnamate is the same enzyme's other substrate, and Rhea gives the two reactions separate masters, but no marker in any namespace separates them: KEGG names the orthologue a 3-phenylpropionate/trans-cinnamate dioxygenase and NCBIfam NF042946 carries the same dual name. Curating cinnamate as a second GIFT would create two traits with identical evidence, so it is deliberately not curated and cinnamate is not claimed.
notes: The markers are orthology groups for the substrate-determining subunits; the shared ferredoxin and ferredoxin reductase components of the same system are deliberately not required, because they are interchangeable between systems and are annotated two to three times less often than the subunits they serve, so requiring them would report an annotation gap as a missing capability.

name: 3-(3-Hydroxyphenyl)propanoate to 3-(2,3-dihydroxyphenyl)propanoate
description: Encodes flavin-dependent hydroxylation of the meta-hydroxylated phenylpropanoid to the catecholic one, the second entry into the same ring-cleavage node. A positive call means the genome encodes one complete curated route. It does not mean the compound is encountered, taken up, degraded in situ, or degraded at any rate.
notes: Curated separately from the dioxygenase entry because the substrates differ; KEGG module M00545 ORs the two into one module, which giftr cannot do, since a route must connect the GIFT's own declared boundaries.

name: 3-(2,3-Dihydroxyphenyl)propanoate to 2-oxopent-4-enoate and succinate
description: Encodes extradiol cleavage of the catecholic phenylpropanoid and hydrolysis of the ring-opened product, releasing succinate and 2-oxopent-4-enoate. A positive call means the genome encodes one complete curated route. It does not mean the compound is encountered, taken up, degraded in situ, or degraded at any rate.
notes: Ends at 2-oxopent-4-enoate rather than at pyruvate and acetyl-CoA, so that the shared lower route is composed through the anchor instead of duplicated.

name: L-glutamate and ammonium to L-glutamine
description: Encodes the ATP-dependent amidation of L-glutamate by glutamine synthetase. Glutamine is curated as its own capability rather than as part of ammonium assimilation because it is a required precursor elsewhere in the database -- pyrimidine, pyridoxal phosphate, tryptophan and histidine biosynthesis all consume its amide nitrogen -- and because a genome can carry glutamine synthetase without any glutamate synthase, in which case it amidates glutamate it cannot itself make.

name: Pyruvate to L-alanine
description: Encodes the formation of L-alanine from pyruvate, either by transamination from L-glutamate or by reductive amination with ammonium. KEGG has no module for alanine, and the textbook alanine transaminase orthology group K00814 is annotated in a single bacterial genome, so the trait is curated from the alanine-synthesising transaminases and alanine dehydrogenase instead. Only pyruvate is declared as a boundary: the two routes use different nitrogen donors, so declaring either would claim a requirement that half the routes do not have.

name: Oxaloacetate to L-aspartate
description: Encodes the transamination that turns the citric acid cycle intermediate oxaloacetate into L-aspartate. One reaction, curated as a capability because it is the entry point of the entire aspartate family -- asparagine, the aspartate 4-semialdehyde trunk, lysine, threonine and methionine -- and because three curated GIFTs already declare L-aspartate as an input that nothing in the database produced.

name: L-aspartate to L-asparagine
description: Encodes the ATP-dependent amidation of L-aspartate, by the ammonia-dependent ligase AsnA or by the glutamine-hydrolysing synthase AsnB. Only aspartate is declared as a boundary: the two routes differ in nitrogen source, and unlike the methionine pair -- where sulfide and cysteine are genuinely different nutritional situations -- ammonium and the glutamine amide are interchangeable intracellular nitrogen, so the difference does not justify two capabilities.

name: L-aspartate 4-semialdehyde to meso-diaminopimelate
description: Encodes the diaminopimelate branch from the aspartate trunk to meso-2,6-diaminopimelate, by any of four alternative routes: succinylated, acetylated, dehydrogenase and aminotransferase. KEGG draws these as four separate modules, each repeating the aspartate kinase and semialdehyde dehydrogenase steps that giftr curates separately, and each scoring badly alone -- 51.4, 5.6, 6.8 and 17.2 per cent of bacterial genomes. As alternative routes of one capability they cover 75.3 per cent, which is what the route layer exists to express. The capability ends at meso-diaminopimelate rather than at lysine because that molecule is also the peptidoglycan cross-link residue.

name: meso-diaminopimelate to L-lysine
description: Encodes the decarboxylation that commits meso-diaminopimelate to L-lysine. Curated separately from the diaminopimelate branch because the two are separately informative: a genome can make the peptidoglycan precursor without making the amino acid, and LysA is present in 85.6 per cent of bacterial genomes while the branch that supplies it completes in 75.3 per cent.

name: Pyruvate to 3-methyl-2-oxobutanoate
description: Encodes the acetohydroxyacid pathway from two pyruvates to 3-methyl-2-oxobutanoate, the branchpoint 2-oxo acid that supplies valine, leucine and pantothenate. Cut here rather than at valine because the same three enzymes also serve the isoleucine branch on a different substrate, so the 2-oxo acid, not the amino acid, is what the evidence identifies -- and because pantothenate biosynthesis already declared this molecule as an input that nothing produced.

name: 3-methyl-2-oxobutanoate to L-valine
description: Encodes the branched-chain transamination that turns 3-methyl-2-oxobutanoate into L-valine. One reaction, curated as a capability because it is the step that establishes valine identity and because the branchpoint before it feeds pantothenate and leucine as well. The same aminotransferase serves leucine and isoleucine, so the marker fires for all three; what separates the three traits is the 2-oxo acid supply, and each of those is separately evidenced.

name: 3-methyl-2-oxobutanoate to L-leucine
description: Encodes the isopropylmalate chain extension that adds one carbon to 3-methyl-2-oxobutanoate, followed by transamination to L-leucine. Extended past the module boundary, which stops at 2-oxoisocaproate, because the amino acid is the capability a reader is asking about and the transamination is the same enzyme already curated for valine.

name: Pyruvate to 2-oxobutanoate
description: Encodes the citramalate route to 2-oxobutanoate, which reaches the isoleucine precursor from pyruvate without passing through threonine. Rare -- 3.3 per cent of bacterial genomes -- and curated because it is the only isoleucine route available to a genome that cannot make threonine, which is exactly the case a composition graph should be able to answer.

name: 2-oxobutanoate to L-isoleucine
description: Encodes the isoleucine branch of the acetohydroxyacid pathway, from 2-oxobutanoate to L-isoleucine. The four enzymes are the same ones that build valine from two pyruvates; the reactions are different because the substrate is. Cutting at 2-oxobutanoate is what makes the two amino acids separable, and it is also what connects isoleucine to its two suppliers: threonine deamination and the citramalate route.

name: Chorismate to L-phenylalanine
description: Encodes the prephenate dehydratase branch from chorismate to L-phenylalanine. The final transamination is evidenced by a wider marker set than KEGG uses: requiring TyrB alone calls the trait in 2296 bacterial genomes where the discriminating aryl skeleton is present in 7796, and accepting the aspartate and branched-chain aminotransferases -- which do transaminate aromatic 2-oxo acids -- recovers 7733. The step is kept required because it is real chemistry, but the specificity of the claim rests on the skeleton, not on the transaminase.

name: Chorismate to L-tyrosine
description: Encodes the prephenate dehydrogenase branch from chorismate to L-tyrosine, with NAD- and NADP-dependent routes that are separately evidenced by different orthology groups. The final transamination carries the same widened marker set as phenylalanine biosynthesis, for the same measured reason.

name: Chorismate and L-glutamine to L-tryptophan
description: Encodes the five-step branch from chorismate to L-tryptophan. L-glutamine is declared as an input because the anthranilate synthase amidotransfer is the nitrogen source of the ring in every route, which is the same reading of an amidotransferase already applied to pyrimidine and pyridoxal phosphate biosynthesis; L-serine, which supplies the side chain, is not, because it is a co-substrate of the last step rather than the boundary the trait is about. The indole intermediate of tryptophan synthase is channelled between the two subunits and never released, so this GIFT does not connect to the indole anchor.

name: PRPP and L-glutamine to L-histidine
description: Encodes the ten-step pathway from PRPP to L-histidine. The module boundary is kept unchanged because the pathway has no stable intermediate that another capability consumes, which is the test for a cut. L-glutamine is declared as an input for the imidazole glycerol-phosphate synthase amidotransfer; the AICAR released by the same reaction is not declared as an output, on the precedent of L-homocysteine, because it is an internal participant of purine core biosynthesis and an edge there would assert a composition nobody would read as biology.

name: L-glutamate to L-proline
description: Encodes the phosphorylation, reduction, spontaneous cyclisation and second reduction that turn L-glutamate into L-proline. L-glutamate is declared as an input here, unlike in the transamination-dependent GIFTs of this layer, because its carbon skeleton becomes the product.

name: L-glutamate to L-ornithine
description: Encodes the acetylated branch from L-glutamate to L-ornithine, by either the linear route that hydrolyses the acetyl group off or the cyclic route that transfers it back onto glutamate. The cyclic ArgJ route is the dominant one outside the Enterobacteriaceae, and the two are separately evidenced. The LysW-carrier route of Thermus and the archaea is not curated: its distinguishing orthology group is annotated in no bacterial genome.

name: L-ornithine to L-arginine
description: Encodes carbamoylation of L-ornithine to L-citrulline, condensation with L-aspartate and elimination of fumarate to give L-arginine. L-citrulline stays internal: the arginine deiminase pathway passes through the same molecule in the opposite direction, and declaring it would assert a composition edge between a biosynthetic and a catabolic capability that share one reversible enzyme rather than a metabolite boundary.

name: L-arginine to L-ornithine and ammonium
description: Encodes the arginine deiminase pathway: deimination of L-arginine to L-citrulline, phosphorolysis back to L-ornithine, and substrate-level phosphorylation of ADP from the carbamoyl phosphate released. The trait most users mean by arginine catabolism, and the principal acid-resistance and ATP-generating strategy of streptococci, lactobacilli and many oral and vaginal taxa. All three components are required: ornithine carbamoyltransferase alone is shared with arginine biosynthesis running the other way, so it is the deiminase and the carbamate kinase that identify the catabolic pathway. L-citrulline stays internal, which is why this GIFT and arginine biosynthesis share no boundary except the two amino acids themselves.

name: L-histidine to L-glutamate and ammonium
description: Encodes the histidine utilisation pathway from L-histidine to L-glutamate: non-oxidative deamination, hydration, ring hydrolysis and release of the formyl group as formamide. Curated with the formamide-releasing hydrolase rather than the folate-dependent formiminotransferase, because the transferase route ends in the one-carbon pool, which giftr has no anchors for.

name: L-threonine to 2-oxobutanoate and ammonium
description: Encodes the PLP-dependent deamination of L-threonine. The chemistry is catabolic wherever it runs, and the same enzyme serves the first step of isoleucine biosynthesis: curating it once, as catabolism, and letting isoleucine biosynthesis compose from the 2-oxobutanoate anchor is what keeps one reaction in one GIFT. The resulting threonine-to-isoleucine chain crosses modes, which is the case the composition rule anticipates.

name: L-serine to pyruvate and ammonium
description: Encodes the deamination of L-serine to pyruvate, the step that makes serine a fermentable substrate rather than only a biosynthetic product. Its product is the pyruvate anchor, so it connects the amino acid layer to the whole fermentation layer in one edge.

name: L-glutamate to 4-aminobutanoate
description: Encodes the PLP-dependent decarboxylation of L-glutamate to GABA. The reaction consumes a cytoplasmic proton, which is why it is the core of glutamate-dependent acid resistance; the product is also the most studied microbially produced neuroactive compound. giftr claims the encoded decarboxylation only: the antiporter that makes the system work as acid resistance is transport chemistry this layer does not curate, and no evidence layer here says whether GABA leaves the cell.

name: L-tryptophan to indole, pyruvate and ammonium
description: Encodes tryptophanase, the beta-elimination that releases indole from L-tryptophan. One reaction, one orthology group, and the strongest host-signal claim in the amino acid layer: bacterial indole is an aryl hydrocarbon receptor ligand that modulates epithelial barrier function, and the reaction is what the classical clinical indole test detects. Curated as a capability on the same grounds as cytidylate biosynthesis: a single transformation that establishes a product identity nothing else in the database produces.

name: L-methionine to methanethiol and 2-oxobutanoate
description: Encodes methionine gamma-lyase, which releases methanethiol, 2-oxobutanoate and ammonium from L-methionine. Methanethiol is a principal volatile sulfur compound of oral malodour and a documented colonocyte irritant. The enzyme is promiscuous towards homocysteine and cysteine; the GIFT is named for methionine and its marker is deliberately not accepted as evidence for any cysteine capability.

name: L-cysteine to hydrogen sulfide and pyruvate
description: Encodes the dedicated cysteine desulfidases that release hydrogen sulfide, pyruvate and ammonium from L-cysteine. The trait is knowingly under-called: many PLP enzymes carry this activity as a side reaction, and accepting them would make every transsulfuration genome a sulfide producer, since cystathionine beta-lyase is already curated as evidence for cysteine biosynthesis. Only the dedicated desulfidase orthology groups are accepted, which is a claim about specificity rather than about prevalence. The product closes the sulfide anchor, which two biosynthesis GIFTs consumed and nothing produced.

name: Glycine to acetyl phosphate and ammonium
description: Encodes the glycine reductase complex, the reductive half of Stickland fermentation: glycine is reduced and deaminated to acetyl phosphate, which phosphorylates ADP. The complete selenoprotein complex is required, which is what makes the trait specific -- 128 of 10151 bacterial genomes -- and it is diagnostic of proteolytic Clostridia including Clostridioides difficile. giftr states the encoded chemistry only: selenocysteine incorporation itself is a separate capability this layer does not evaluate.

name: L-proline to 5-aminopentanoate
description: Encodes Stickland proline reduction: racemisation of L-proline to D-proline and reductive ring opening to 5-aminopentanoate by the selenoprotein proline reductase. The racemase is required because the reductase is specific for the D isomer, and the two together are what distinguishes the trait from proline oxidation. Rare and diagnostic, like glycine reduction, and it forms a cross-mode pair with proline biosynthesis.

name: Mercury detoxification
description: Encodes the machinery that detoxifies mercury by reducing Hg(II) to volatile elemental Hg(0), through the NADPH-dependent mercuric reductase MerA, with delivery of the metal to the reductase, mercury-responsive induction of the operon and organomercurial carbon-mercury lysis as accessory functions. A positive call means the genome encodes MerA-dependent reduction. It does not mean the organism survives mercury exposure: that depends on the dose, on which mercury species it meets, and on efflux and sequestration systems this GIFT does not describe.
notes: Reduction is the only required function. A genome carrying merA alone detoxifies the Hg(II) that reaches its cytoplasm, which is the claim; requiring merT and merP would refuse such a genome on the strength of an operon architecture that varies, because merC and merE substitute for the pair in several lineages, and giftr has no evidence layer for how much metal gets in. Organomercurial lysis by MerB is curated as an accessory function and not as a second mechanism: broad-spectrum resistance is a genuinely different phenotype, and whether it deserves its own mechanism is recorded as an open question in inst/doc/proposal-aromatic-degradation.md. Mercury methylation by hgcAB is not this capability and is not curated: it makes mercury more toxic, not less.

name: Isocitrate to 2-oxoglutarate
description: Encodes oxidative decarboxylation of isocitrate to 2-oxoglutarate by either NADP- or NAD-dependent isocitrate dehydrogenase. A positive call establishes the oxidative fate of the isocitrate branchpoint; it does not mean the citric acid cycle closes.
notes: Separated from acetyl_coa_to_isocitrate so that the glyoxylate bypass can branch at a declared anchor without duplicating the upper segment. The two cofactor-specific reactions are alternative routes because their markers distinguish them.

name: Isocitrate and acetyl-CoA to succinate and malate
description: Encodes the two-reaction glyoxylate bypass: isocitrate lyase cleaves isocitrate to succinate and glyoxylate, then malate synthase condenses the glyoxylate with acetyl-CoA to malate. A positive call means this carbon-conserving branch is encoded. It does not mean the glyoxylate cycle closes, carries flux, or supports growth on any substrate.
notes: Isocitrate is the branch boundary; glyoxylate is produced and consumed inside the complete route and remains internal. K01639 is refused because it is N-acetylneuraminate lyase, not malate synthase. K19282 is deferred because its malyl-CoA route requires two different Rhea reactions rather than the direct malate-synthase reaction curated here.

name: Dinitrogen to ammonium
description: Encodes reduction of dinitrogen to ammonium by a complete curated nitrogenase architecture, including the catalytic and electron-delivery components and the nitrogenase-specific cofactor-assembly proteins that cannot be replaced by housekeeping pathways. A positive call means the genome encodes nitrogen-fixation chemistry. It does not mean the system is expressed, protected from oxygen, supplied with reductant, or fixes nitrogen in situ.
notes: The molybdenum architecture requires NifHDK, NifEN and NifB; NifU, NifS, NifV and NifM are not required because their roles are not universally nitrogenase-specific or can be supplied by host pathways. A vanadium architecture requires VnfHDGK, VnfEN and NifB and is a separate route with its own Rhea master. NifH alone is explicitly insufficient. The Fe-only architecture is deferred because current KO groups do not separate AnfHDK from NifHDK while the minimum native assembly requirement remains context-dependent.

name: Sulfate to hydrogen sulfide
description: Encodes activation and assimilatory reduction of sulfate to hydrogen sulfide through either the direct APS or the PAPS branch and either NADPH- or ferredoxin-dependent sulfite reductase. A positive call means one complete assimilatory route is encoded. It does not mean sulfate is available, sulfur is incorporated into biomass, or dissimilatory sulfur respiration occurs.
notes: Four minimal routes materialise the APS/PAPS and NADPH/ferredoxin alternatives. The shared CysH KO K00390 is refused because KEGG assigns it both EC 1.8.4.8 and 1.8.4.10 and it cannot decide which branch is complete; the two branch reactions therefore use reaction-specific EC markers. Dissimilatory AprAB and DsrAB markers are not accepted. CysNC is represented at the correct system layer as a fusion that can satisfy APS kinase and, with CysD, sulfate adenylyltransferase.
